claim_ceiling: This is a local measurement at the two named commits, on this machine. It is not a universal claim about the test suite.
A passing count does not license a claim that the product works; it only bounds the code change between two commits.
The excluded modules are still unexecuted. Their RF3 tracked-results writer defect is recorded separately in results/product/regression/tracked_results_writer_inventory.json.

collection_scope.why_excluded: These modules import sentence_transformers/torch, which is not installed in the CI or bare image. They are excluded identically at baseline and at head, so the comparison is a set relation over the same population. Excluding a DIFFERENT set at baseline and head would invalidate the delta.

delta.derived_not_asserted: net_new_passing_tests is head.passed - baseline.passed, computed here. It is never written into a report by hand; RF2's '+7' defect was a hand-written delta that disagreed with the two counts it came from.

numeric_environment.warning: Recorded because a from-source rebuild is environment-scoped, not byte-identical across machines (BLAS reduction order). A count that differs run-to-run on the SAME commit is an environment signal, not evidence of a code change - re-measure before publishing a delta.

pinning_rule: A pin names a run id and a commit sha. It is never a timestamp and never a re-probed moving snapshot, because a timestamp names an instant rather than a tree: the same command re-run later legitimately differs, so the pin cannot be checked and rots silently. If a pin cannot be made correct, this tool exits non-zero instead of repinning.
what_this_is: Commit-anchored test accounting. Replaces both the hand-written delta (RF2: '+7' published where the measured change was '+10') and the timestamp pin (RF4: a 21:30:00Z snapshot was already stale against a 22:24:12Z re-probe). Every delta below is computed from the two measured counts, never written by hand.
